horizon_risk.caveat: Reduced to 200 Monte Carlo paths (vs. the retired 6-leg script's 2000) for runtime reasons -- disclosed, not hidden; see project_wheel_v1_horizon_risk.py's own module docstring. This is the FIRST run of this exact Monte Carlo methodology at the new T1=70% policy -- it has not been iterated/cross-checked across multiple runs the way the old script was over time. Read alongside, not instead of, the reconciled REAL backtest numbers: $2,372,248.48 final / 162.45% CAGR / -30.0% MDD over the real 4-year window, $6,354,608.73 / 124.27% CAGR / -36.8% MDD over the real 6-year window (T1=70%, active policy). The prior T1=30% policy's own real numbers ($939,296.63/108.19%/-28.2%/4yr, $1,479,308.37/75.89%/-27.3%/6yr) remain the retained comparison benchmark. T1=70%'s robustness study found this dominance is real but fragile: it loses to 30% in the real 2018-2020 window, and under >=25% T1 edge degradation or severe execution-cost stress -- ongoing monitoring of T1 edge deterioration (signal expectancy, execution quality, trade frequency) is recommended.
horizon_risk.policy: Wheel v1.0 (T1=70% active policy since 2026-10-27, adopted after a 3-part robustness study): D2 reversible leverage ladder (3x/4x/5x/6x, 15% hysteresis) -> permanent switch to C30-B's rule (3x/4x) the first time equity reaches $500,000 (never reverts). Original T1=30% policy retained as a comparison benchmark, not deleted -- see wheel_v1_shadow_engine.py's LEGACY_* constants.
